sources.fullCitation: “Leonard Whitcup has been appointed managing director of Music, Music, Music, Inc., publishers of S/Sgt. Barry Sadler’s songs. In his new post, Whitcup will be responsible for developing new talent and writers. Whitcup, who is also a songwriter, is currently executive vice-president of the American Guild of Authors & Composers.” With a portrait captioned “Whitcup”. Billboard, 14 May 1966, p. 3. World Radio History.
sources.title: Executive appointments: Leonard Whitcup
sources.creator: Billboard
sources.researchNote: The notice supplies two offices that no other record gathered for him gives: managing director of the publishing house Music, Music, Music, Inc. from May 1966, and executive vice-president of the American Guild of Authors and Composers at that date. It also confirms that the man in the trade press is the songwriter, which is what ties this likeness to the composer of the American song that enters the Kaper record in 1932. The portrait stands thirty-four years after that song.

media.title: Leonard Whitcup — portrait, Billboard, 14 May 1966
media.description: Portrait of the songwriter Leonard Whitcup printed with the trade announcement of his appointment as managing director of the publishing house Music, Music, Music, Inc., captioned simply “Whitcup”.
media.altText: Head-and-shoulders portrait of a bespectacled man in a dark suit and patterned tie.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The trade paper of 1966 is within the term of United States copyright and the archive that supplies the scanned issue asserts no free licence; no photographer or agency is credited beside the portrait. The local 228 × 268 pixel reproduction is used for the identification of the sitter alone, with the paper, the archive and the unresolved permission stated alongside it.
